kurz: Dissolved substances move by themselves to where there is less of them. But only slowly, a few millimetres in hours.
bild_im_kopf: Like a drop of ink spreading slowly in water, only much slower, because meat is not water.
was_passiert: Salt, sugar and aromas move from the surface to the inside. Small molecules such as salt manage this in hours to days; large aromas and oil barely get in. That is why marinades mainly season the surface.
warum_wichtig: Explains why salt soaks in but marinade aromas stay on the outside, and why braises taste better the next day.
faustregeln: Salt works its way inside over time, but most flavours in a marinade stay on the outside. Marinades mainly season the surface.
Yesterday's stew: the aromas have had time to spread.
